successCriteria.description: All 6 methods in EmployeeRepository (findById, findByEmployeeNumber, findAll, create, update, softDelete) use only Knex chainable query builder API — zero `this.db.raw()` calls remain in the file.
findById returns Employee | null: uses `.select('*').where('id', id).whereNull('deleted_at').first()`, maps row via toEmployee, returns null (not undefined) when no row found.
findByEmployeeNumber returns Employee | null: uses `.select('*').where('employee_number', employeeNumber).whereNull('deleted_at').first()`, maps via toEmployee, returns null when no row found.
findAll returns Employee[]: uses `.select('*').whereNull('deleted_at')`, maps all rows via toEmployee, returns empty array when no rows.

create returns Employee: builds an insert object with snake_case keys from domain fields + createdAt/updatedAt set to `new Date()`, calls `.insert(row).returning('*')`, extracts first row, maps via toEmployee.

update returns Employee | null: first checks existence via findById (returning null if absent), builds a dynamic update object from the column map filtering out undefined values and always adding updated_at, calls `.update(obj).where('id', id).whereNull('deleted_at').returning('*')`, extracts first row, maps via toEmployee. Returns existing employee unchanged when no fields to update.
softDelete returns void: calls `.update({ deleted_at: new Date(), updated_at: new Date() }).where('id', id).whereNull('deleted_at')`, does not return rows.

All existing Jest tests pass with semantically identical assertions — mock infrastructure may change to support chainable API, but every test's expected return values, null/empty cases, and parameter assertions remain equivalent.

constraints: The IEmployeeRepository interface must not change — method signatures, parameter types, and return types remain exactly as declared.
The Employee model interface must not change — all field names, types, and optionality remain exactly as declared.
